response.rationale: Four T1 sources and one T2 source all point the same way: the Li 2010 and Lyster 2010 meta-analyses report durable corrective-feedback effects, and Butler 2007 finds feedback improves final-test performance (delayed feedback beat immediate feedback). I discounted the Adesope 2017 and Hattie 2007 entries because their text is identical, so they are probably not independent. That text also reads like a product-policy statement ("no retrieval surface ships without...") rather than a finding. Even so, the first three sources support the claim.
